newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW Australia winter crop seen progressing well.
newsitem.headline: NSW Australia winter crop seen progressing well.

text.p: Winter crop sowings were well underway on a greater area than last year in the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW), the NSW Agriculture Department said in its latest grains report on Wednesday.
An estimated 4.13 million hectares of winter crops had been sown this year compared with about 4.02 million ha harvested in 1996, it said.
Canola plantings were up by 30 percent this year to 192,000 ha, it said.
Further rains in mid-May had been ideal to progress sowings, it said.
Harvest of the estimated 535,000 hectares of summer crops was nearing completion, with generally dry, favourable weather, it said.
Excellent average summer crop yields were predicted, with record maize production and the biggest soybean crop this decade, it said.
No effective rain fell in the grains belt during April.
In most areas there had been no rain since early March and in some areas since December last year, it said.
Useful rains were received in early May on the southwest slopes, in the Murray valley and in parts of the central west, permitting significant winter crop sowings, it said.
Other areas received very scattered falls, sufficient for sowing of a minor area, it said.
Widespread rains of 15 millimetres to 30 millimetres were received during mid-May, allowing sowings to progress in most areas, it said.
Mild conditions should enhance early growth, while there was a good storage of sub-soil moisture in many districts.
"A general air of optimism prevails with winter crop producers spurred on by predictions of reasonably profitable grain prices for 1997 harvested grain," it said.
Wheat sowings are estimated at 2.7 million ha compared with the 1996 harvested area of 2.8 million ha.
Barley sowings are estimated at 582,000 ha against an estimated 517,000 ha last year and a record 623,000 ha in 1993.
Pulse sowings for 1997 would possibly total 154,000 ha against 106,000 ha harvested last year, it said.
Summer crop sowings excluding rice were estimated at 535,000 ha, up seven percent on last season, it also said.
An estimated 280,000 ha of cotton would be harvested this season to produce about 1.9 million 500 pound bales of lint. Maize production was expected to reach a record high of 244,000 tonnes.
Soybean production at 63,000 would be the biggest this decade, with harvest virtually complete.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
